newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Jet dips, sparking new demand.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Jet dips, sparking new demand.

text.p: Singapore jet levels dipped, enticing fresh bids while gas oil rose tracking firmer swaps quotes, traders said on Wednesday.
The return of buyers in both markets sparked cautious optimism that prices are at the start of an uptrend.
Focus shifted towards the jet market after Tuesday's gas oil trades. Two jet cargoes changed hands with a August 14-18 loading supplies traded at $22.60 and another for August 15-19 at $22.50.
The former was sold by a Dutch trader and the latter by a US major. Both cargoes were purchased by a western trader.
The same trader about ten days ago purchased an early August cargo from Kuwait at a 10-15 cents premia to Singapore spot quotes fob Singapore.
Traders said the outright deals traded were significantly lower from Tuesday's quotes which was offered lowest at $22.60.
The low levels have also enticed other end users to emerge.

A South Korean seller was heard to have sold a 30,000 barrels cargo at 20 cents premia to Singapore spot quotes, fob South Korea. India has also emerged to buy a 30,000 tonnes, 15-30 August cargo at 60 cents over middle east spot quotes.
Comparatively, the gas oil market was thin. The local trader which emerged late Tuesday to buy two cargoes were absent, traders said.
Traders said the local trader has been supporting the swaps market while pricing out cargoes to Indonesia and taking advantage of the wide differential between swaps and cash prices.
Traders said cash fundamentals continue to be weak. They said regional gas oil demand is still weak.

"Chinese market is dead, the barge market in Hong Kong have come to a standstill. The clamp down on the smuggling is very harsh and it has affected oil trade very badly, said one oil major in Hong Kong.
"We are not offering any cargoes, most traders are adopting a wait and see attitude," he said.
Chinese traders said stocks in northern China are high and most refiners are considering reducing runs.
Moaming refinery has already cut runs at its 170,000 barrels-per-day refinery by about 10-15 percent.
The jet fuel/gas oil spread or regrade is narrow in response to the surging gas oil prices and weak jet fuel fundamentals where there are by fears of a prompt overhang, traders said.
The August regrade was last quoted at 10/30 cents per barrel, down from 40/60 cents on Tuesday.
